objective: Produce deterministic human-like whole-body deformation from rig pose and declared contact/load state, independent of exercise names.
clean_room_rules: No external skinning, muscle, character or solver source code is copied into production.
External literature may justify general mathematical/biomechanical principles only; all production implementation and data are independently authored.
No third-party character geometry, scan, weight, corrective, texture or bind data enters ORIGINAL v1.
Legacy V-series implementation data remains historical/reference-only and is not a production source.
hard_invariants: No deformation driver may branch on an exercise name.
Every deformation decision is a deterministic function of current rig transforms, candidate-owned deformation data, and explicitly declared contact/load facts.
Base skinning mode is evidence-selected and must match Blender/runtime parity; it is not changed globally because one academic method is theoretically better.
Anatomical coupling is evaluated before cosmetic correctives.
Weights-only/base-skinning deformation must be plausible enough that correctives refine rather than conceal foundational attachment errors.
Every multi-anchor tissue system uses all relevant proximal/distal attachment state; one moving bone may not wholesale-own the shared tissue.
Corrective interpolation must be continuous through outbound, intermediate and return motion.
No candidate is accepted from endpoint-only examples.
The same joint state must produce the same deformation regardless of which exercise generated it.
Runtime and Blender reference deformation must agree within an explicit later parity tolerance; no hidden Blender-only feature may remain at production freeze.

stack.name: Canonical skeletal kinematics
rules: Uses validated joint construction and coupled girdle/limb motion.
No surface correction is allowed to conceal a true skeletal-motion defect.

stack.name: Evidence-selected base skinning
stack.output: base deformed surface before anatomical corrective layers
rules: Record exact Blender Armature modifier settings for each evaluated candidate.
Do not switch LBS/DQ/hybrid globally without candidate-bound A/B evidence across the whole stress/movement matrix.
Base skinning is not anatomical acceptance; shared-tissue coupling still applies.

stack.name: Multi-anchor anatomical coupling
driver_features: anchor distance or path-length ratio where meaningful
neighboring joint state for multi-joint tissues
rules: Coupling fields are generic by tissue system, not by exercise.
Proximal and distal attachment neighborhoods remain rooted to their anatomical anchors.
Interior ownership transitions are spatially smooth and candidate-audited.
Lengthening/compression, volume redistribution and fold logic are coupling outputs to prove, not assumptions.

stack.name: Generic joint-state pose-space corrective layer
interpolation_requirements: defined outside exact authored sample poses by declared extrapolation/clamping policy
allowed_driver_examples: humerothoracic elevation plus plane of elevation
hip flexion plus knee flexion for biarticular posterior/anterior thigh systems
knee flexion plus ankle angle for gastrocnemius/Achilles-related response
rules: Corrective bases are authored/solved only after base and coupling evidence identifies the residual.
A basis mode must have declared vertex scope, mirror rule, source candidate and evidence.
Intermediate and reversal sampling are mandatory to reject overshoot/popping.
Multiple corrective modes compose under an explicit deterministic order or additive/local-frame rule.

stack.name: Contact/load-aware local response
rules: Contact state may affect hand/palm/wrist and foot/forefoot/heel local response where evidence supports it.
Contact deformation may not move skeletal anchors to hide a contact error.
No contact response may violate the declared whole-chain load path.

stack.name: Optional secondary soft-tissue dynamics
inputs: bone velocity/acceleration history if later justified
rules: Secondary jiggle/inertia is not required to hide incorrect quasi-static anatomy.
If implemented, it must be first-party, deterministic under the selected simulation/update contract, bounded, and return-stable.
Production may freeze without this layer if the product target does not require visible secondary dynamics and the owner accepts the quasi-static result.

generic_driver_contract.determinism: Same permitted input state and candidate data must yield bitwise-stable or declared numeric-tolerance-equivalent deformation on the same implementation target.
generic_driver_contract.evidence_rule: Each driver is validated across its state domain, including interpolated interior states and reversal, not only authored extrema.

base_skinning_selection_gate.decision_rule: Select by whole-body evidence. Neither LBS nor DQ/preserve-volume is assumed globally superior; a hybrid is permitted only if independently implemented and better supported across the complete matrix.

requirements: same pose-space corrective bases and driver definitions
candidate/runtime data hashes bound in evidence
cross-runtime surface comparison over mandatory movement samples
production_parity_gate.production_blocker: Any Blender-only deformation mechanism not reproducible by the first-party runtime blocks production freeze.

research_design_lessons.citation: Kavan et al. (2007), Skinning with Dual Quaternions
research_design_lessons.permissible_lesson: Linear blend skinning has known joint/twist artifacts; nonlinear base skinning is a candidate to test, not a production dependency.

research_design_lessons.citation: Kim and Han (2014), Bulging-free dual quaternion skinning
research_design_lessons.permissible_lesson: Dual-quaternion skinning has its own bulging/normal artifacts; do not assume DQ alone solves human anatomy.

research_design_lessons.citation: Kim et al. (2011), Pose space parameterization and style transfer of skin deformation
research_design_lessons.permissible_lesson: Joint-state parameterization can drive continuous example-based skin deformation; independently author our own driver/basis system.

research_design_lessons.citation: Yang and Zhang (2006), Automatic muscle generation for character skin deformation
research_design_lessons.permissible_lesson: Anatomy-informed muscle bulging/sliding can complement skeletal skinning in complex regions; no external implementation or muscle geometry is copied.

research_design_lessons.citation: Murai et al. (2017), Dynamic skin deformation simulation using musculoskeletal model and soft tissue dynamics
research_design_lessons.permissible_lesson: Dynamic/secondary tissue response is a distinct later layer; it should not be confused with fixing quasi-static attachment anatomy.
